title: Unique Number of Occurrences
spaceBreakdown:
- unordered_map<int,int> cnt: up to n entries → O(n)
- unordered_set<int> seen: up to n entries → O(n)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vector
approach: Count how many times each value appears using a hash map. Then iterate over the frequency values and use a hash set to detect if any frequency appears more than once. If a frequency is already in the set, return false; otherwise return true. This works because the answer is true exactly when all occurrence counts are distinct.
hints: If you listed how many times each distinct value appears, what property of that list tells you the answer is true?

Use a hash map to count occurrences of each value, then a hash set to detect duplicate counts. For arr = [1,2,2,1,1,3], the map gives {1→3, 2→2, 3→1}; inserting 3, 2, 1 into the set finds no duplicates, so return true.

```
count = empty map
for each x in arr:
    count[x] += 1

seen = empty set
for each (value, freq) in count:
    if freq in seen:
        return false
    add freq to seen
return true
```

**Single element** - The array has only one element, so there is exactly one occurrence count.
`Input: arr = [5]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: returning `cnt.size() > 1` as the success condition → returns false

**Two values, same count** - Two distinct values each appear exactly once.
`Input: arr = [1,2]` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: inserting the map key into the set instead of the count → no collision detected → returns true

**All elements equal** - Every element is the same value.
`Input: arr = [7,7,7]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: returning false when `cnt.size() == 1` → returns false

**Negatives and zero** - Values include negative numbers and zero.
`Input: arr = [-3,0,1,-3,1,1,1,-3,10,0]` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: using a fixed array indexed by `arr[i]` without adding an offset for negatives → out-of-bounds access → undefined behavior

followUps.q: What if the array arrives as an unbounded stream and cannot fit in memory?
followUps.a: You still need all counts finalized before checking for duplicates, so store counts in an on-disk hash map or use external sort then count consecutive runs. After collecting all frequencies, load them in batches and use a hash set to detect duplicates. TC: O(n log n) for external sort, SC: O(k) where k is the number of distinct values that fit in memory at once.

followUps.q: What if arr[i] can be any 64-bit integer instead of being bounded to [-1000, 1000]?
followUps.a: The hash map approach already handles arbitrary integer keys without modification, since unordered_map hashes any int type. No algorithmic change is needed. TC: O(n) expected, SC: O(n).

followUps.q: What if you must use O(1) extra space (beyond modifying the input)?
followUps.a: Sort the array in place, then scan consecutive runs to compute each frequency. Collect run lengths back into the array, sort them in place, and check for adjacent duplicates. TC: O(n log n), SC: O(1) auxiliary (input is modified in place).
